summary.intent: Continue and complete GSD Phase 70.1 (rotation read-plane durability and crash-resume soundness) through wave-based parallel execution, get the D-16 desktop-e2e acceptance checkpoint green on macOS/Linux/Windows, verify the phase goal, and run the full ship-phase flow (verify/secure/validate/simplify/SDK-E2E/CodeRabbit/ship).
summary.outcome: All 13 plans merged, three real product bugs found and fixed (depth-3 decrypt-before-dirtiness-check in both engines, JsonSidecarFloorStore multi-writer race, and a scope-exit revocation bypass + double-publish), D-16 went green on all three platforms, phase verification passed (7/8 SC fully verified, SC#6 closed via live sdk-e2e), and the ship-phase flow got through Verify/Secure/Validate/Simplify/SDK-E2E gates plus CodeRabbit triage (2 confirmed findings fixed with TS+Rust parity, 1 refuted) — PR opening and final review-resolution steps were still in progress when the transcript ends.

repo: rust-analyzer diagnostics (dead_code, E0063 'field missing', unresolved import) are frequently stale mid-edit snapshots in this repo during concurrent agent edits — always confirm with authoritative `cargo check`/`cargo test` before trusting them.
gsd commit helper can report `commit_failed` as a false negative while the commit actually lands — verify via `git log`, never blindly retry.
`cargo fmt --all` in an executor strands out-of-scope formatting drift across unrelated files; always scope to `cargo fmt -p <crate>`.
Cross-package dist staleness causes false test failures after a wave merge — rebuild sdk-core+sdk dist before re-running consumer vitest suites.
sdk-e2e vitest has no dotenv loader; TEST_LOGIN_SECRET/env must be sourced into the shell (`set -a; . ./.env; set +a`) before running, or login 401s.

macOS FUSE-T defers file `release` by ~40s and the publish queue is edge-triggered (drains only on a subsequent FUSE op) with no wall-clock backstop — an idle mount can silently never republish a parent folder.

Cross-Client Sync Test 5/7 macOS soft-skips are a separate READ-side bug: FUSE-T ignores the `inval_inode` reverse-notification so the SMB client cache serves stale content even after correct server-side re-resolution — distinct from the write-side publish-queue-drain issue.
Windows exit code -1073741502 (0xC0000142/STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED) on a desktop-e2e API-start step is a transient Windows CI runner flake, not a code issue — re-running the job alone resolves it.

Two rust-analyzer processes eating ~11GB total can be caused by a stale/orphaned editor+RA process bound to a deleted worktree directory (e.g. leftover from a prior phase) parented by an old `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` session — kill the orphan process tree to reclaim RAM.

CodeRabbit CLI (`coderabbit review --agent --base main --type committed`) can misattribute root cause (e.g. blaming an unreachable 'missing parent' path) while still correctly flagging the real defect (per-child fail-open) — always adversarially re-verify CLI findings against actual code before fixing.

code.finding: collectDirtyFrontier now checks childPub.generation > childRef.generation BEFORE calling unsealChildReadKey — dirty edges are pushed with nodeReadKey: undefined and never decrypted, fixing a bug where decrypting a stale sealed ref with the parent's rotated key threw CryptoError.
Rust twin of the TS decrypt-before-dirtiness-check fix: collect_dirty_frontier checks generation before attempting unseal.

JsonSidecarFloorStore::new() previously built its own private Arc<Mutex<()>> per instance even when multiple instances (generation/seq/checkpoint stores) pointed at the same rotation-high-water.json sidecar, causing a concurrent-rename race (ENOENT). Fixed with a process-global path-keyed lock registry (shared_lock_for) so co-located instances share one lock.

rotate_read_on_scope_exit originally discarded the RotateReadResult (matched Ok(_)) and never refreshed the grant-root inode's in-memory read_key, so a subsequent relink resealed the folder under the STALE pre-rotation key — a revocation bypass letting a cut-off recipient still decrypt. Fixed by capturing RotateReadResult and calling refresh_grant_root_read_key to update the inode in place.

build_scope_exit_child_override failed OPEN per-child (child-not-found -> continue; build_child_refs error -> warn+skip) unlike its fail-closed sibling build_folder_metadata, and the override REPLACES the grant-root's published child list — a transient lookup failure could silently drop a sibling from the folder, causing silent data loss with no EIO. Fixed by propagating those two error cases while preserving the two legitimate skip cases (non-File/Folder children, never-published children).

The resume Skipped-branch discarded VerifySubtreeOutcome.is_dirty (kept only .frontier), so a missing/unresolvable root (is_dirty:true, frontier:[]) could be mis-marked Complete instead of routing to the fail-closed resolve. Currently dormant in production (FUSE persist_job is a no-op so completed_node_ids never repopulates) but a real latent soundness gap in the resume path; fixed to check !is_dirty before short-circuiting, mirrored in the TS engine.ts reference.

WinFsp coalescing was ported via a new shared run_scope_exit_gate_coalesced function (also used by fuser delete.rs) so the fuser and WinFsp delete paths can't drift; suppress-signal is stored on a new CipherBoxFS.coalesced_scope_exit_relink_suppressed HashSet since WinFsp splits delete across set_delete->cleanup.

workflow: When a canary-first (single-plan-then-fan-out) approach is used for wave parallelism, explicitly tell the user upfront — silently doing so reads as 'not actually parallel' and draws direct pushback.
Hold/batch multiple independent fixes (e.g. WinFsp port + macOS drain fix) and push them together in one CI dispatch rather than burning a ~30min real-mount CI cycle per fix.

When resuming a debugger/investigator agent that already holds full root-cause context (file line numbers, reproduced evidence, a written FakeTransport test), resuming via SendMessage is far cheaper than spawning a fresh agent that must re-derive the same context.

Always verify a subagent's summary claims against the live checkout before trusting them — multiple 'diagnostics show X is broken/unused' claims from agents turned out to be stale editor snapshots, confirmed clean by authoritative `cargo check`.

For a phase with TS+Rust engine parity as an explicit goal, any fix discovered in one engine must be checked and mirrored in the other before considering the fix complete — CodeRabbit findings prompted checking TS parity for a Rust-only bug and found the identical latent defect there.

friction: Multiple stale rust-analyzer / mid-edit-snapshot diagnostics (E0063 missing struct field, dead_code, unresolved macro reference) required repeated authoritative cargo check/test verification cycles to rule out false alarms, costing time each time.

GSD commit helper repeatedly reports commit_failed as a false negative (lint-staged hooks are slow on large files like ROADMAP.md, sometimes exceeding the 2-min Bash timeout), requiring manual git log verification each time rather than trusting the tool output.

desktop-e2e CI round-trips are slow (~15-40 min per run across 3 platforms) and multiple issues had to be discovered serially across several dispatched runs (macOS setup timeout -> revocation bypass/double-publish -> Windows coalescing gap -> Windows API-start flake) before D-16 went fully green.

local live idle-mount validation of the macOS publish-queue-drain fix was impossible on the interactive dev machine because background Spotlight/Finder processes generate spontaneous FUSE ops that mask the exact bug being fixed, forcing reliance on CI as the only valid test bed.

TEE-worker-dependent tests (tee-republish.test.ts) failed during the SDK-E2E ship gate due to an unseeded local tee_key_state — an environment-setup gap unrelated to the phase, requiring investigation to rule out as a regression.
Two orphaned rust-analyzer processes bound to a deleted worktree (leaked from a stale Phase-69 Claude session) were silently consuming ~5.4GB of RAM until the user noticed and asked about it.
open_items: WinFsp handle_rename ungated-dest D-15d parity gap — tracked in .planning/todos/pending/2026-07-08-winfsp-d15d-gate-ordering-parity.md (delete path now closed; rename path still has the pre-existing ordering issue).
Desktop query_grants_rooted_at is a no-op — ROT-04 inner grant re-mint on desktop is deferred, tracked in .planning/todos/pending/2026-07-08-desktop-query-grants-rooted-at-remint-noop.md.

macOS FUSE-T read-side cache invalidation gap causing Cross-Client Sync Test 5 (content sync) and Test 7 (folder rename sync) to soft-skip on macOS — tracked in .planning/todos/pending/2026-07-09-macos-fuse-t-cross-client-sync-invalidation.md; requires either a working FUSE-T notification path or a shorter SMB cache TTL.

queue.rs duplication (identical floor-sidecar-skip guard block copy-pasted in load_all_for_vault and gc_failed_entries) flagged by the simplify reviewer as low-value; deliberately not refactored to keep ship-phase scope tight.

Finding 3 (CodeRabbit) — borrowed (non-copied) IPNS/owner/write key buffers passed by reference from client.ts into the rotation engine are not currently zeroed by the engine (refuted as a live defect) but remain a latent hardening opportunity (defensive copy at the seam) not applied.

Stale/dangling Phase-69 checkout and its orphaned Claude session/rust-analyzer process were cleaned up manually mid-session but the root cause (worktree cleanup not killing associated processes) was not addressed as a systemic fix.
Ship-phase flow was mid-execution at transcript end: PR not yet opened, PR review resolution and final CI-green confirmation and learnings-extraction steps (Steps 8-11 of ship-phase) still pending.
